author: OElNino
quote:
GTA VI - Overhyped Masterpiece or Disappointing Reality ?

It was expected to redefine gaming and set a new standard for open-world experiences. While Rockstar has delivered an impressive world with incredible visual detail, several decisions and problems deserve serious criticism.

1. The 30 FPS limitation
One of the biggest disappointments is the 30 FPS cap, even on PS5 Pro. In 2026, a game of this scale and budget should offer a 60 FPS performance mode. Visual quality is important, but smooth gameplay and responsiveness should not be sacrificed entirely for graphics.

2. Physical editions without discs
Selling physical editions containing only digital download codes defeats the purpose of buying a physical copy. Reports of missing or already-redeemed codes have also raised concerns. Even more controversial are reports that codes could potentially be visible through certain packaging using a flashlight, creating a possible security issue.

3. Excessively positive reviews
The overwhelmingly positive professional reviews raise questions about critical standards. When critics award almost perfect scores while user ratings are dramatically lower, it creates a significant credibility gap. User reviews can be unfair, but professional reviewers should not treat a technically impressive game as automatically flawless.

4. Technical problems and bugs
Reports of crashes, disappearing weapons, lost character statistics, clipping, visual glitches, strange physics and other gameplay issues are disappointing for a production of this scale. A massive budget and years of development should translate into a more polished experience.

5. Restrictive mission design
Despite its enormous open world, GTA VI reportedly continues Rockstar's traditional problem of restricting player freedom during missions. Scripted sequences, limited approaches and excessive mission constraints can make an otherwise open experience feel surprisingly linear.

6. Pacing and excessive realism
The focus on everyday activities, lengthy conversations and relationship development between Jason and Lucia may improve immersion, but can also make the experience unnecessarily slow. Realism should enhance entertainment, not replace it.

7. No PC version at launch
Excluding PC players at launch is another questionable decision. A significant part of the gaming community has to wait, while console players are limited to 30 FPS. For a release of this magnitude, a simultaneous PC launch would have been preferable.

8. Price and consumer expectations
After years of hype, enormous marketing campaigns and premium pricing, expectations are understandably high. Consumers should not have to accept technical compromises, questionable distribution methods or unfinished features simply because the game carries the Rockstar name.

Final Verdict
GTA VI is undoubtedly an impressive technical and artistic achievement (so are others), but that does not make it immune to criticism. The 30 FPS limitation, performance issues, questionable physical editions, digital licence concerns, reported bugs and restrictive gameplay decisions deserve proper scrutiny.

The biggest problem may be the culture surrounding the game itself. Some players defend every Rockstar decision, while others criticise everything without giving the game a fair chance. A game should be judged by its actual quality, not by its reputation, marketing budget or hype.

GTA VI should be held to a higher standard precisely because it is one of the most anticipated and expensive games ever made. 

Being a Rockstar production should not grant it immunity from criticism!

Happy plays everyone! For GTA VI or any other game :)
